==English== [[Image:Ice Tea.jpg|thumb|300px|right|Ice tea '''poured''' into a glass]] ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|pô|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/pɔː/}} * {{enPR|pôr|a=GenAm}}, {{IPA|en|/poɹ/}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-pour.ogg|a=US}} * {{enPR|pōr|a=rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}}, {{IPA|en|/po(ː)ɹ/}} * {{IPA|en|/poə/|a=non-rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}} * {{q|obsolete}} {{enPR|pour|pouər}}, {{IPA|en|/paʊɹ/|/paʊəɹ/}}{{R:Critical Pronouncing Dictionary|entry=Pour|page=422|ipage=1}} * {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|pore|;|poor|;|paw}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|pouren|t=to pour}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Perhaps from {{der|en|fro-nor|purer|t=to sift (grain), pour out (water)}}, from {{der|en|la|pūrō|t=to purify}}, from {{m|la|pūrus|t=pure}}. Compare {{cog|dum|afpuren|t=to pour off, drain}}. {{m|en||To pour}} displaced several Middle English verbs: * {{m|enm|schenchen}}, {{m|enm|schenken|t=to pour}}, from {{noncog|ang|sċenċan|t=to pour out}} and {{noncog|non|skenkja}}, from {{noncog|gem-pro|*skankijaną}}. Compare dialectal {{m+|en|shink}}, {{m|en|skink}}. * {{m|enm|yeten}}, from {{m+|ang|ġēotan|t=to pour}}, from {{noncog|gem-pro|*geutaną}}. * {{m|enm|birlen|t=to pour, serve drink to}}, from {{m+|ang|byrelian|t=to pour, serve drink to}}. * {{m|enm|hellen|t=to pour, pour out}}, from {{m+|non|hella|t=to pour out, incline}}. * {{m|enm|temen|t=to pour out, empty}}, from {{m+|non|tœma|t=to pour out, empty}}. Compare archaic {{m+|en|teem#Etymology 2|teem}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[cause]] (liquid, or liquid-like substance) to flow in a [[stream]], either out of a [[container]] or into it. #: {{ux|en|'''pour''' water from a jug}} #: {{ux|en|'''pour''' wine into a decanter}} #: {{ux|en|to '''pour''' oil onto chips}} #: {{ux|en|to '''pour''' out sand or dust.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|figurative}} To [[send]] out as in a stream or a flood; to [[cause]] (an emotion) to come out; to cause to escape. #: {{ux|en|My teacher '''poured''' scorn on my attempts at writing.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 5|5|prologue|passage=How London doth '''pour''' out her citizens.}} #* {{RQ:King James Version|1 Samuel|1|15|passage={{...}} I haue drunke neither wine nor strong drinke, but haue '''powred''' out my soule before the Lord.}} #* {{RQ:King James Version|Ezekiel|7|8|passage=Now will I shortly '''powre''' out my furie vpon thee, and accomplish mine anger vpon thee{{...}}}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1637|author=w:John Milton|title={{w|Comus (Milton)|A Mask presented at Ludlow Castle, 1634}}|text=Wherefore did Nature '''pour''' her bounties forth / With such a full and unwithdrawing hand?|section=lines 710-711}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-10|volume=408|issue=8848 |title=[http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21583277-worlds-biggest-polluter-going-green-it-needs-speed-up-transition-can-china Can China clean up fast enough?] |passage=At the same time, it is '''pouring''' money into cleaning up the country.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[send]] [[forth]] from, as in a [[stream]]; to [[discharge]] [[uninterruptedly]]. #* {{RQ:Pope Essay on Man|passage=Is it for thee the linnet '''pours''' his throat?}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[flow]], [[pass]]{{,}} or [[issue]] in a [[stream]]; to [[fall]] [[continuously]] and [[abundantly]]. #: {{ux|en|the rain '''poured''' down.}} #* {{quote-song|en|author=w:Taylor Swift;w:Imogen Heap|authorlabel=no|title={{w|Clean (song)|Clean (Taylor's Version)}}|album=w:1989 (Taylor's Version)|date=27 October 2014|date_published=27 October 2023|artist=Taylor Swift|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RKAXdSe8MYM|text=The rain came '''pouring''' down
When I was drownin', that's when I could finally breathe}} # {{lb|en|impersonal}} To [[rain#Verb|rain]] [[hard]]. #: {{synonyms|en|spate}} #: {{ux|en|It's '''pouring''' outside.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} Of a beverage, to be [[on tap]] or otherwise [[available]] for serving to [[customers]]. # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To move in a [[throng]], as a crowd. #: {{syn|en|sweep|crowd|throng}} #: {{ux|en|The people '''poured''' out of the theater.}} #* {{RQ:John Gay Trivia|passage=In the rude throng '''pour''' on with furious pace.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=January 8, 2011|author=Chris Bevan|work=BBC |title=[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/9341711.stm Arsenal 1-1 Leeds] |passage=In a breathless finish Arsenal '''poured''' forward looking for a winner but Leeds held out for a deserved replay after Bendtner wastefully fired wide and Schmeichel acrobatically kept out Denilson's rasping effort}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To move (a [[drunk]] or [[unsteady]] person) into or out of a place or [[vehicle]]. #: {{ux|en|She '''poured''' him into a taxi and handed the driver the fare.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=1954-10|author=Juanita Sheridan|title=There Are No Snakes in Hawaii|journal={{w|Ellery Queen's Mystery Magazine}}|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/Ellery_Queens_Mystery_Magazine_v24n04_American_Mercury_Oct_1954/page/n53/mode/2up|page=51|text=“Was he really drunk?” I asked. “He was stiff!” Bill Garrison told us from the steps. “We just '''poured''' him into the car and Mavis took him home.”}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1994|author={{w|Nora Roberts}}| title=The Best Mistake| chapter=9| isbn=9780727889270| passage=When Coop '''poured''' himself out of the cab and staggered towards the house, he already knew he'd hate himself in the morning.}} #* {{quote-av|en|writer={{w|John Finnemore}}|title={{w|Cabin Pressure (radio series)|Cabin Pressure}}|season=4|number=1|episode=Timbuktu|date=2013-01-09|network={{w|BBC Radio 4}}|text=Did any of you order a furious posh man? {{...}} Very cross, very drunk. Phil '''poured''' him into your departure hut.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2016|author={{w|Martina Cole}}| title=Betrayal| isbn=9781472201041| page=198 |pageurl=https://archive.org/details/betrayal0000cole/page/198/mode/2up| passage=When Tony got in he listened to her going on incoherently about how Aiden had finally fucked up and, as always, he agreed with her and '''poured''' her into bed.}} =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|pour a drink}} {{l|en|shink}}, {{l|en|skink}} =====Derived terms===== {{col3|en|title=Terms derived from ''pour'' Choo|title=Advanced concrete technology: Volume 2 |passage=Over this time period, the first concrete '''pour''' has not only lost workability but has started to set so that it is no longer affected by the action of a vibrator.}} # {{lb|en|colloquial}} A [[downpour]]; a [[flood]] of [[precipitation]]. #* {{RQ:Beckett Watt|text=But then one of Mr. Knott's men would have had to put on his coat and hat and turn out, as likely as not in the pitch dark, and in torrents of rain in all probability, and grope his way in the dark in the '''pours''' of rain, with the pot of food in his hand, a wretched and ridiculous figure, to where the dog lay.}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|med pour|rainpour}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|a stream, or something like a stream; a flood}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Portuguese: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|a flood of precipitation}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Japanese: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== ====Verb==== {{head|en|verb}} # {{misspelling of|en|pore}}. ===References=== {{reflist}} ===See also=== * {{l|en|pour encourager les autres}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=opru|puro|roup}} {{C|en|Liquids}}
